title: Fifth difference: effects—mortal falls bring heavier losses under the grace-covenant than lighter faults
source_text: XLVI. Quinto peccata mortalia a venialibus differre affirmat ratione effectuum qui peccati actus consequuntur, hoc est, ratione detrimenti quod peccantibus afferunt; quia calamitates & damna, quae ex peccatis mortalibus fidelibus accidunt, multo gra-viora & tristiora sunt iis quae consequuntur peccata leviora, sive venialia. Postea vero singillatim exponit tria mala sive damna, quae mortalia renatorum sequuntur, juxta vero dispensationem providentiae divinae sub foedere gratiae, non sequuntur peccata leviora ab ipsis commissa.
pass_a_gloss: Fifthly he affirms that mortal sins differ from venial by reason of the effects which follow the act of sin—that is, by reason of the detriment they bring upon sinners; because the calamities and damages which befall the faithful from mortal sins are much heavier and sadder than those which follow lighter or venial sins. Afterwards indeed he sets forth one by one three evils or damages which follow the mortals of the regenerate, yet which according to the dispensation of divine providence under the covenant of grace do not follow the lighter sins committed by them.
pass_b_english: Effects differ: mortal falls cost the regenerate far more than daily lighter faults.
Baron will track three covenant-ordered damages that trail mortal—not venial—slips.
